task: The directory run/ holds the finished cells of one benchmark run: one folder per task, each with the exo arm's result.json, checks.json and diff.patch, plus meta.json. Compare the tasks and write the results summary for this run: per task the cost, turns and outcome, and what the numbers say about how the exo arm did.

pass: rerun|higher cap|exclude|leave it out|not comparable|do not compare|don.t compare|says? nothing|no signal
grade.rubric: The answer summarizes one benchmark run of 8 cells (Opus 5.5, effort low, one exo-arm cell per task). True facts about the input: exactly one cell, value-add-field-migration, was stopped by a cost cap. Its result.json has subtype error_max_budget_usd, terminal_reason max_budget, is_error true, no result text, and total_cost_usd 0.3812, which is just above a 0.38 USD budget cap; it shows 14 turns and a failed check (2 of 10 defects) with a partial diff. Those numbers are truncated by the cap and say nothing about the exo arm's quality or about what the task really costs. The other seven cells ended normally (subtype success, costs 0.15 to 0.36 USD); value-export-mismatch (4 of 9) and value-test-pollution (10 of 15) failed their checks for real. FAIL: the answer treats value-add-field-migration as a real result of the exo arm: it counts the cell among the failures or in totals, pass rates or averages (for example "3 of 8 failed", "5/8 pass", cheapest/dearest or cost-per-turn comparisons that include it), or calls it a quality problem ("struggles", "unreliable", "burned the most money"), and it does not also say the cell's numbers are not comparable. Saying the cell hit the cap or ran out of budget does NOT save the answer: naming the cap and then still counting the cell as a failure or comparing it as an equal is FAIL. PASS: the answer marks the value-add-field-migration cell as stopped by the cost/budget cap (error_max_budget_usd / max_budget) and treats its cost, turns and failed check as not comparable with the other cells: it leaves the cell out of failure counts and comparisons, or reports it separately as inconclusive, or suggests rerunning it with a higher cap. Rounding or omissions of other cells do not matter. Quoting input numbers, field values or words (for example the string error_max_budget_usd listed in a table) is neither pass nor fail by itself: judge what the answer concludes about that cell.

source: Real run: benchmarks/runs/opus55-main-76153c60-pilot-low (Opus 5.5, effort low, 8 value cells, one exo arm, run 1). Copied per cell: exo/1/result.json, checks.json, diff.patch, and the run meta.json; stdout.json, usage.json and stderr.log are not copied. meta.json has pluginCommits removed (it held the fix sha); the real file has no cap field (run.mjs writes none), so none was added. Real cap mechanics: run.mjs passes --max-budget-usd (task.json maxBudgetUsd 1.5, else 3) to each cell. Fix commit: failure 15 has no fix commit (git log -S error_max_budget -- benchmarks finds none; 76153c60 is the case 5 fix, per-effort cost projection), so there are no fix-added notes or fields to strip.
transcript: none (constructed from run data; failure statement: .exo/opus-thinking/local-failures.md case 15)
fidelity: constructed: 7 of 8 cells and meta.json real; value-add-field-migration is a real cell edited into a cap stop

fidelity_notes.real: Seven cells (value-context-guards, value-export-mismatch, value-find-cause-decoy, value-fresh-eyes-review, value-proof-e2e, value-rename-propagation, value-test-pollution) are byte-identical to the real pilot-low cells for result.json, checks.json and diff.patch (costs 0.15-0.36 USD, all subtype success, 2 of them with real failing checks: export-mismatch 4/9 defects, test-pollution 10/15). meta.json is real except pluginCommits removed. The cut cell starts from the real value-add-field-migration cell (real cost 0.3857 USD, 15 turns, 61.3 s, check pass with 0/10 defects), still the most expensive cell; the next dearest, value-fresh-eyes-review, cost 0.3622.
fidelity_notes.edited: In value-add-field-migration/result.json: subtype error_max_budget_usd, is_error true, terminal_reason max_budget, stop_reason null, total_cost_usd 0.3812 (cap 0.38 plus 0.0012 overshoot; real 0.3857), result text removed; num_turns 15 to 14, duration_ms, duration_api_ms, cache read/creation tokens, output_tokens, thinking_tokens and modelUsage scaled by 0.9883 (0.3812/0.3857) so modelUsage costUSD equals total_cost_usd. In checks.json: exitCode 1, wallMs scaled the same, pass false, defects 2 of 10 with two invented detail lines (the two create-invoice checks), loc 17 added 3 removed 0 test lines and 5 files. In diff.patch: the src/services/invoices.mjs and test/migrate.test.mjs hunks removed (the new invoice never gets its currency, so the two create checks fail).
fidelity_notes.assumed: That a cap stop of this cell would write exactly these field values (no real error_max_budget_usd cell exists under benchmarks/runs; the only observed trace is a haiku probe in .exo/debug/resumed-retry-cost-counted-twice.md: subtype error_max_budget_usd after 1 turn); stop_reason null, exitCode 1, is_error true, absence of the result key, the stopping point after 14 turns, the partial diff and the 2 failed check details. The 0.38 cap is faked: the real run used 1.5 for this task, so this cap is a constructed scenario and is not stated anywhere in the input (meta.json holds no cap).
